slides.title: Flex Items Can Behave Differently 🎭
slides.content:
# Individual Control

While the container sets rules for all, each flex item can override alignment, sizing, and order. The key properties:
- `order` – changes the visual order without altering HTML.
- `flex-grow` – ability to grow to fill extra space.
- `flex-shrink` – ability to shrink if needed.
- `flex-basis` – the initial main size before growing/shrinking.
- `align-self` – overrides `align-items` for that single item.

slides.title: `order`: Rearrange Without HTML Changes 🔄
slides.content:
# Source‑Order Independence

`order` accepts an integer (default 0). Items are laid out in ascending `order` value. Negative values allowed.

```css
.item:first-child {
  order: 1; /* moves to the end */
}
```
Use sparingly – visual order should match the DOM for accessibility, unless absolutely necessary.

quizData.question: By default, what is the `order` value of flex items?
quizData.explanation: All items have `order: 0;` by default, maintaining source order.

slides.title: `flex-shrink`: Shrinking When Space Is Tight 📉
slides.content:
# Shrink Factor

`flex-shrink` (default 1) determines how much an item shrinks relative to others when container is too small. 0 means don't shrink.

```css
img {
  flex-shrink: 0; /* never shrink image */
}
```
Useful for preserving icons or fixed‑size elements.

slides.title: `flex-basis`: The Starting Size 📏
slides.content:
# The Initial Main Size

`flex-basis` sets the size before growing/shrinking. Can be a length (px, %) or `auto` (look at width/height). Default is `auto`.

```css
.item {
  flex-basis: 200px; /* start at 200px then grow/shrink */
}
```
If `flex-direction` is row, it's width; if column, it's height.

slides.title: `align-self`: Override Cross Alignment 🧘

quizData.question: Which property prevents a flex item from shrinking?
quizData.explanation: Setting `flex-shrink: 0;` stops the item from reducing its size below its flex‑basis.
